Retain e2fc28947c38 adaptation of the memory-pressure forward-progress requirement on native per-page allocation: no blocking page allocation while holding an unsubmitted partial bio or recursive submit context; submit partial bios with a remaining reference, queue empty allocation failures to WQ_MEM_RECLAIM, and save matching residual iterator/DUN. records.rationale: Retain the small final Android legacy wrapped-key UAPI/KDF adapter already integrated at 2fbc2da4ade3. Pinned vold KeyUtil.cpp explicitly emits __flags for kHwWrappedV0 because upstream and legacy identifiers/on-disk policies differ; libfscrypt parses wrappedkey_v0 separately. This is active userspace format compatibility, not historical vendor binary KMI. Native size, flags, v2-only, provisioning-key, capability, wiping and hardware-secret-provider checks remain. Exception: legacy keys deliberately use the raw-key identifier KDF context, weakening native raw/wrapped identifier domain separation; someone possessing the derived software secret can obtain the same identifier by adding it as raw, potentially affecting key claims/removal/re-add semantics. No claim that this reveals the hardware contents key. Modern wrapped-key requests retain native separation. SDK fstab selects raw AES-XTS/CTS without inlinecrypt or wrappedkey_v0, and native derive_sw_secret requires inlinecrypt plus a supporting hardware profile; current SDK activation is unverified and not asserted. Conservatively retain this generic current Android API, record unresolved necessity, and add no platform-specific support. See SECURITY.md for the explicit security tradeoff.
